real_estate.homebuilder: Outside the gas pump, Bay Area living costs are rising modestly, and rents here rose just 2.6% in a year.
real_estate.commentary:
This week's spending headlines, translated for the Bay Area: September prices rose 3.7% from a year ago nationally, but one item did much of the damage. Gasoline cost 34% more than a year ago, and 31.5% more here. Leave out food and energy and prices rose 2.6%.

Housing is the good news locally. Bay Area rents rose 2.6% from a year ago, a touch below the nation's 2.8%, and shelter costs overall rose 2.6% here versus 3.2% nationally. Groceries are the one place the Bay Area runs hotter, up 4.4% here versus 1.8% nationally, and car insurance costs 5% less than a year ago.

Mortgage rates closed the week steady. MND's 30-year ended Friday at 7.37% and the 15-year at 7.04%. On our five city median list price of $1,088,000 with 20% down, principal and interest run about $6,009 a month.

Locally, the five city ledger reads 679, down from 687, as Fremont slipped to 233 from 237 and Union City to 64 from 66. The board wide table eased to 2,666 from 2,681, while brand new listings rose to 210 from 196.

What this means for you: a paycheck rising about 3% a year is keeping up with everything but the gas tank, and Bay Area rents are rising slower than that. Buyers have room to negotiate, with 169 homes on the five city ledger listed 60 days or longer.

• Board wide: 2,666 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 136 coming soon and 210 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 679 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 609 are on the market and 70 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 233 live, 186 active, 27 coming soon, 17 brand new and 3 back on market. The median on market list price is $1,298,500 at $804 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 37 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 188, Milpitas 100, Newark 94, Union City 64.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,088,000 at $681 a square foot. 283 homes are priced under a million, and 169 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

stocks.news:
Stocks ended a choppy week mixed. The Dow finished up 0.67% for the week, while the S&P 500 lost 1.95% and the Nasdaq 4.48% as investors sold chip and AI shares. Friday's drop was led by AMD (down 5.95%), Micron (down 5.63%) and CoreWeave (down 11.91%), while energy stocks rose with oil.

The consumer side looks healthier than the tech tape. September sales at online retailers rose 8.2% from a year ago and at restaurants 7.0%, a good sign for retailers heading into the holiday quarter. Netflix kicks off a busy earnings week on Tuesday.

economy.note: Markets are closed for the weekend. Gold and silver are Friday, October 16 settlements (COMEX December); Brent is Friday's ICE December settlement; the 10-Year is Friday's Treasury close.
economy.commentary:
Shoppers kept spending in September. Retail and restaurant sales rose 0.8% from August and 6.3% from a year earlier, the Census Bureau said Thursday, and Reuters reported the gain beat expectations. Restaurants and bars took in 7.0% more than a year ago while menu prices rose 3.5%, so people are eating out more, not just paying more.

Gasoline did a lot of the lifting. Gas station sales jumped 6.4% in the month and 28.1% from a year ago, while pump prices rose 34.2%, so drivers paid more for slightly less fuel. Leave gas stations out and sales still rose 4.5% from a year ago. Higher spending does not always mean buying more, and at the pump it did not.

Some of the scarier graphics online this week show a grocery cart up 10%. The September data puts grocery prices up 1.8% nationally and 4.4% in the Bay Area, and car insurance down 5%. Average hourly pay rose 3.0% over the year: behind the 3.7% rise in all prices, mostly because of gasoline, but ahead of the 2.6% rise outside food and energy.

Oil rose again Friday, with Brent settling at $109.86, up 3.72%, as tanker attacks around the Strait of Hormuz picked up. That keeps gasoline the line item to watch, and also the one that can ease fastest when oil cools.

feature_image.alt: Paired bar chart, September 2026 vs a year earlier. All stores and restaurants: sales up 6.3%, all consumer prices up 3.7% (buying more). Restaurants and bars: sales up 7.0%, menu prices up 3.5% (buying more). Grocery stores: sales up 0.9%, grocery prices up 1.8%. Gas stations: sales up 28.1%, gasoline prices up 34.2%.
feature_image.caption: Overall and at restaurants, sales grew faster than prices, so shoppers bought more. At the pump and the grocery store, prices outran sales.
feature_image.source: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Advance Monthly Retail Sales (Oct. 15, 2026); U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPI-U. Store sales are matched to the main item each store type sells.
